content:
This page describes how the Swarm Support Watcher, a Discord application operated by the Swarm Foundation, handles data on the official Swarm Discord server. The effective date of this policy is 2 September 2026.

What the bot is

The Swarm Support Watcher helps the Swarm Foundation's Developer Relations team notice and answer community questions faster. It reads new messages in a fixed list of public support and discussion channels, identifies messages that likely need a reply from the team (questions, support requests, mentions of the team), and forwards each flagged message to a private team coordination channel, together with a suggested draft answer generated from Swarm's public documentation.

The bot never posts, replies, or reacts in Discord. Every answer a community member receives is written and sent by a human team member.

What data it reads

  • New messages in a fixed allowlist of public channels on the Swarm Discord server (support and discussion channels such as node-operators and builders). It does not read private channels, channels it has no permission to see, or direct messages.
  • For each message: the message text, the author's public username, the channel name, and a link to the message.
  • Messages written by bots are ignored.

What it does with the data

  • Messages are screened automatically to decide whether they need a team reply. Screening uses simple rules plus an AI classification step (Anthropic's Claude API). Message excerpts are sent to that API for classification and drafting; Anthropic does not use API data to train its models.
  • For flagged messages only, a short excerpt (up to 240 characters), the username, the channel name, and a link are forwarded to a private, invite-only team coordination channel visible to Swarm Foundation team members.
  • Answers approved by the team may be kept as generalized question-and-answer notes so future draft answers improve. These are internal working notes and are not published.

What it does not do

  • It does not post or react anywhere on Discord.
  • It does not build profiles of users, track presence or activity, or read member lists.
  • It does not sell or share data with third parties. The only processors involved are the infrastructure the bot runs on and the Anthropic API used for classification and drafting.
  • It does not store full channel history. Only flagged messages are stored, as short excerpts.

Retention

Stored excerpts and their handling status are deleted 14 days after a question is resolved. Generalized approved answers may be kept longer as team knowledge; they do not include message links or usernames where those are not needed.

Your choices

  • The bot only operates in the listed public channels. Anything you post elsewhere on the server is not read by it.
  • If you would like a specific message of yours removed from the bot's records, contact the team on Discord or at info@ethswarm.org and it will be deleted.

Contact

Questions about this policy: info@ethswarm.org, or ask a moderator on the Swarm Discord. The general privacy policy for the ethswarm.org website is at /privacy.
